items.title: George Guesnon Interview, 1965-09
items.q: I mean, Lawrence, I mean, I tried to break him with that. It became too much of a monotonous thing.

ctx.x: he say, I'd go to Duke Ellington's band. I like this. From the Eureka magazine. A much more satisfactory four-four beat, as is the playing of, in the LP under Robinson's name. Geno is much better than Marrero. His rhythm playing is lighter and harder for him. Yeah, I think what I'm sure. And he plays jazz solos, well constructed and melodic.

That's quite true. Well, I mean, well the Cressnos, like I say, you seek for more, you find more. I mean, Lawrence, I mean, I tried to break him with that. It became too much of a monotonous thing. Everything was too, heavy. And it just never, the change never stroked. You know what I mean? The stroke never changed. I mean, it was, you see, but you don't have to play like that. Instead of trying, you judge from your wrist. Uh-huh. Of what you must do. When they become loud, when they get soft. Yeah. That's right.…

That's done with the wrist, you see. While I'm, you see, while I'm picking, I'm easing up on the vibration on the wrist. I mean, that's right. Do you think you ever have, have you ever been better than just that time?
